page.layout: One page of running text in a single column; margin note in the right margin beside the paragraph on Ariæi and the Gauls. Running head at top; page number at top right; catchword at bottom right.

main_text.p: perta ovain terra fœtum ederent, teste Aristotele & Plin.

Bonosus imperator, ut scribit Flavius Vo-piscus, bibit, quantum alius nemo: & si quando legati barbarorum gentium vndecunq; venif-fent, ipsis propinauit, vt eos vino obrueret, fic-que ab ebriis consilia eliciebat.
Protheas Macedo apud Alexandrum bibacissimus fuit, & valenti corporis robore, tandé tamen vino periit.
Illyrii cubantes cœnabant & bibebant, teste Periandro &c.
Scythas, Iberos, Thraces, Gallos, Persas & Lydios vinolentiæ deditos fuisse Plato prodidit.

Stratage-ma Gal-lorumAriæi conuiuia celebrabant quotidie, & inebriabantur, quare Galli, qui bellum aduersus eos gerebant, id animaduertentes, dolum co-menti sunt. Singuli enim Gallorum duces prandium exquisitissime in tabernaculis suis apparauerunt, cibariisq; adiecerunt herbam quandam medicamentosam quæ aluum deiiciendi & violenter purgandi vim obtineret: vnde quotquot ex iis ediffent, ad vnum extin-cti sunt omnes.

Præterea & flumina eadem herba infecerant, quæ postea hausta aluum immodice purgarunt. Constat certe multos & inuictos exercitus militum vinolentiâ fuisse prostratos. Germanis nostris olim in bello Gal-lico simile quid accidisse plusquam notu est.

page.notes: The running head reads "PRoEOGANDA", probably PROLOGANDA; the letters are uncertain. The page number "59" is partly worn at the top right. The catchword "Car-" is clear. The word "sunt" after "extin-cti" is doubtful. The margin note is printed in three lines, "Stratage- / ma Gal- / lorum", and is transcribed as one note with its printed hyphens. Long s is written as plain s throughout, and v/u and j/i follow the modern convention.
